title: Live-check the wallpaper stretching under a frosted bar
description:
The live gate from issue #6 was waived by the owner so PR #8 could merge. The
code path was audited by reading, not by running. This issue tracks the
outstanding on-machine verification.

Why it was skipped: the review session has no WAYLAND_DISPLAY or NIRI_SOCKET,
so `niri msg` is unreachable there, and swapping the owner's live wallpaper
backend from a non-interactive shell is out of bounds.

What the merge already established by reading the code:

- `internal/wayland/owner.go:512` passes `LayerSpec.ExclusiveZone` straight into
  `SetExclusiveZone` with no clamping, and `LayerSpec.Width/Height` stay 0, so
  `SetSize(0,0)` leaves the extent to the compositor.
- The generated binding writes `uint32(-1)` (0xFFFFFFFF) little-endian; the
  protocol declares the argument as `int` and its doc comment names -1 as the
  wallpaper value ("stretch below or over the panel").
- All geometry flows from the compositor configure into `ConfiguredGrid`, with
  no hardcoded top/left inset for a larger surface to disagree with.

Still unverified: that Niri actually reports the full output for a zone -1
Background surface, and that a frosted bar samples effect pixels rather than an
empty strip.

Procedure, per AGENTS.md: record the current wallpaper assignment before
starting, restore it when finished.

1. Enable the frosted bar with blur-behind on.
2. Run the engine and confirm effect pixels are visible through the bar strip
   instead of a flat empty band.
3. Run `niri msg -j layers` and confirm the Background surface reports
   full-output geometry.
4. Restore the owner's previous wallpaper assignment.

If any of the three fails, reopen issue #6 rather than patching around it.
acceptance_criteria: Effect pixels visible through the frosted bar strip; niri msg -j layers reports full-output geometry for the Background surface; owner's previous wallpaper assignment restored afterwards.
notes:
Owner reports frosting absent with terminal-effect wallpapers (2026-10-11). Niri 26.04 (8ed0da4) advertises blur; shell 27fddeae logs blur available and includes 0b684039 (40% frost/pill floor for playing or paused effects). Both outputs mapped sysc-terminal Background surfaces during inspection. niri msg layers exposes no dimensions, so this does not prove full-output coverage.

Installed engine was v0.1.0 at 5af2f666, with LayerSpec.ExclusiveZone = 0. That allows panel insets and predates the -1 fix, making missing pixels beneath the bar the first thing to verify. Updated the installed executable through CGO_ENABLED=0 go install from clean origin/main 0d7959b; its catalog has 13 standalone effects. Existing wallpaper processes were not restarted for an experiment. A newly selected effect uses the update.

Next: compare current-main effect coverage beneath the bar with a still on each output, then check bar BlurShape, transparency and configured geometry. If coverage is correct but frost still fails, compare xray on/off for sysc-shell:bar and sysc-shell-panel, including repaint after effect frames and after pause/resume. Niri 8ed0da4/src/niri.rs:update_xray_render_elements includes Background layer surfaces, so unsupported terminal surfaces are not an established cause. Record settings, screenshots and compositor logs. Restore the owner assignment and config after any experiment. Keep the original geometry and visibility acceptance gate open until live evidence passes.

title: Engine has no per-glyph font fallback, so braille effects blank out on fonts without braille
description:
The rasterizer holds a single *font.Font and does not check glyph coverage. drawGlyphCell falls back to gid 0 (.notdef) when NominalGlyph fails, and raster() returns an empty Alpha for an empty outline, so a missing glyph paints a blank cell instead of erroring.

This became load-bearing when PR #7 merged the logo-spin family: all four of those effects emit braille (U+2800-U+28FF) as their only output. A probed font without braille coverage renders them as empty grids.

Origin: the per-glyph fallback work (raster: fall back to other installed faces per glyph) exists on an unmerged branch and is NOT an ancestor of origin/main. internal/raster/font.go does not exist on main.

Fix direction: probe several mono faces (the engine already discovers roots and candidates in internal/wayland/owner.go findFont) and pick the first that has braille; keep the single-font path as the fallback. Verify with a font lacking U+2800.

title: Rasterizer draws block elements from font glyphs, so block art shows seams between cells
description: Kitty draws U+2580-259F block elements and light box lines geometrically, so block art tiles. The rasterizer blits font masks; Fira/JetBrains block glyphs do not fill the integer cell, leaving a grid of seams in effects and in sysc-lock text-effect headers. Fill these runes as exact rectangles in the cell.

title: Kitty background_opacity does not reveal the sysc-terminal wallpaper
description: Reported by owner 2026-10-10: with sysc-terminal as the wallpaper, a transparent kitty window (background_opacity < 1) does not show the effect behind it. Investigate layer, namespace and niri layer-rules (place-within-backdrop / opacity), and whether the wallpaper surface is what niri composites behind windows.
notes: Live probe 2026-10-10 (cross-logo, sysc-logo, rain on DP-1/DP-3, gSlapper restored): kitty DOES blend over sysc-terminal; a gamma-lifted capture shows the cross through the window. Default-bg kitty pixels read (10,10,10) over black canvas vs (27,19,44) over the purple still. Cause is content, not compositing: the engine fills unset cells with opaque black and the nord logo strokes are dark, so kitty's 15% see-through (opacity 0.85) shows almost nothing. Options: paint the theme background instead of pure black, brighten logo palettes, or lower kitty opacity.

title: Evaluate GPU blur for terminal-effect wallpaper frames
description:
Owner requests a quick blur feasibility investigation and explicitly permits GPU rendering (2026-10-11).

sysc-lock has two separate paths: internal/render/blur.go downsamples a frozen pre-lock capture (factor 4) and applies three horizontal/vertical box-blur passes; internal/lockd/effect_gpu.go renders six effects through CGO/EGL/GLES, ping-ponged state textures and glReadPixels into BGRA. The animated GPU path has no blur pass. Its six-effect shader list omits the logo effects and is not a replacement for the sysc-Go registry.

Evaluate a GPU post-processing blur of the existing sysc-terminal frame so all 13 standalone effects retain their authoritative implementation. Compare a reduced-resolution separable shader pass with the existing downsampled CPU blur algorithm. Measure upload, blur, readback, buffer-release latency, RSS and paused work at actual output sizes. Do not assume the locker's GPU gains transfer when CPU-rendered terminal pixels need uploading and reading back.

ext-background-effect blurs content behind a requesting surface; requesting it on an opaque Background wallpaper does not blur the wallpaper's own pixels. Keep this separate from sysc-terminal-1, which investigates shell frosting above the wallpaper.

sysc-lock's GPU backend is internal and uses handwritten C/CGO. Record a Go-compatible binding/ownership option under this repository's current language constraints before implementation; GPU permission is recorded. Keep Wayland proxies on the connection owner and preserve frame-callback/buffer-release pacing, zero work while paused, the CPU fallback and the approved numeric budget. No backend or new dependency added by this investigation.
acceptance_criteria: Source-backed recommendation comparing GPU post-processing with downsampled CPU blur; measured prototype costs before implementation, preserved effect registry and pause/frame invariants, explicit language boundary and resource-budget fit.
notes: Recommendation: use stdlib area averaging and three reduced-resolution separable box passes; wp_viewport scales on the compositor. Maximum strength 64 at 3440x1440 passed CPU p95 26.771 ms against 30 ms cap at approved 120 ms cadence. Retain authoritative sysc-Go effects. No shader backend or dependency required. GPU post-processing remains a fallback if further real-output measurements fail; upload/readback costs have not been measured.

title: Add bounded wallpaper blur and advertise support
description: Owner approved adjustable wallpaper blur on 2026-10-11. Default off; 0..64 output pixels; authoritative sysc-Go frames; pure-Go area averaging and three reduced-resolution box passes with compositor viewport scaling; preserve unblurred dirty-render history, pause/frame/release rules and resource limits. Engine and Settings changes ship as reviewed PRs.
notes: Local review LGTM. Maximum-blur fire/nord hardware gate at 3440x1440: 120 ms cadence, CPU p95 26.771 ms (22.3% of one core), CPU mean 25.114 ms, wall p95 26.541 ms. Named raster/reference, CLI, cadence and pause checks pass; vet and CGO-disabled build pass. Live visual blur and fractional-scale/RSS observations remain unverified.
